CLIMATE NOTE

NOTE
SE MI resides under the dry slot of northern Great Lakes low pressure to start the day limiting any precip to isolated pockets of drizzle. This gradually begins to change through the latter half of the morning mainly towards the Saginaw Valley/Thumb as southwesterly winds draw in moisture off Lake Michigan supporting widely scattered light showers. Chances expand over the southern portions of the CWA late this afternoon as a lobe of vorticity rounds the trough over the area providing a bit more lift to squeeze out scattered light showers which then persist into early tonight. System's secondary cold front sweeps across the region early Friday morning offering a window for better coverage before ushering in a true late fall airmass to close the week out. 850mb temps fall sub 0C behind the front as troughing sinks over the central Great Lakes capping highs slightly below average in the 40s to 50 Friday. The now closed low likewise sinks southeast over lower MI Friday generating a generally unsettled day with periodic showers and breezy northwesterly winds making it feel even cooler than the highs would suggest. Greatest shower coverage/intensity likely focused over the Thumb as the low center tracks nearby wrapping in additional lake moisture. Rain chances gradually winds down over the course of Friday night as troughing shifts towards the eastern Great Lakes. Temperatures remain around early November averages Saturday though will feel cool given the fall thus far. Cloud cover slowly erodes through the day as surface high pressure/drier air slowly expands over the region. Ridging then expected to govern conditions through the first half of the new week promoting another drier stretch and moderation back above normal temperature-wise. && .MARINE... The occluded low pressure system continues to stretch and drift northeast into Ontario and Quebec this morning. The initial cold front has pulled through the region but the lingering stacked upper level and surface troughs will remain draped across the region today. This will keep a southwesterly gradient across the area and continued gusty winds. Deeper mixing in the wake of the cold front brings southwest wind gusts to around 25 kt across Saginaw Bay Thursday so a Small Craft Advisory is in effect through this evening. A stronger cold front then tracks southward across the region on Friday. This brings gusty north and northeast wind that shifts northwest and weakens by Saturday. Additional light rain will accompany this frontal passage. && .PREV DISCUSSION... Issued at 1156 PM EST Wed Nov 4 2026 AVIATION... Upper level trough of low pressure will now be in place over Southeast Michigan throughout the period. Deepening of the cold air with time in the lower troposphere will lift ceilings heights to VFR. Strong midlevel subsidence between 5.0 and 15.0 kft agl will end widespread precipitation Wrap around moisture advection with daytime heating is expected to result in diurnal shower development Thursday afternoon. Most organized of synoptic moisture appears to pivot into the area Thursday evening. DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES... * High for ceiling 5000 ft or less tonight and Thursday. && .DTX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES... MI...None. Lake Huron...Small Craft Advisory until 10 PM EST this evening for LHZ421-422. Lake St Clair...None. .DISCUSSION...

SE MI resides under the dry slot of northern Great Lakes low 
pressure to start the day limiting any precip to isolated pockets of 
drizzle. This gradually begins to change through the latter half of 
the morning mainly towards the Saginaw Valley/Thumb as southwesterly 
winds draw in moisture off Lake Michigan supporting widely scattered 
light showers. Chances expand over the southern portions of the CWA 
late this afternoon as a lobe of vorticity rounds the trough over 
the area providing a bit more lift to squeeze out scattered light 
showers which then persist into early tonight. System's secondary 
cold front sweeps across the region early Friday morning offering a 
window for better coverage before ushering in a true late fall 
airmass to close the week out. 

850mb temps fall sub 0C behind the front as troughing sinks over the 
central Great Lakes capping highs slightly below average in the 40s 
to 50 Friday. The now closed low likewise sinks southeast over lower 
MI Friday generating a generally unsettled day with periodic showers 
and breezy northwesterly winds making it feel even cooler than the 
highs would suggest. Greatest shower coverage/intensity likely 
focused over the Thumb as the low center tracks nearby wrapping in 
additional lake moisture. Rain chances gradually winds down over the 
course of Friday night as troughing shifts towards the eastern Great 
Lakes.

Temperatures remain around early November averages Saturday though 
will feel cool given the fall thus far. Cloud cover slowly erodes 
through the day as surface high pressure/drier air slowly expands 
over the region. Ridging then expected to govern conditions through 
the first half of the new week promoting another drier stretch and 
moderation back above normal temperature-wise.

&&

.MARINE...

The occluded low pressure system continues to stretch and drift 
northeast into Ontario and Quebec this morning. The initial cold 
front has pulled through the region but the lingering stacked upper 
level and surface troughs will remain draped across the region 
today. This will keep a southwesterly gradient across the area and 
continued gusty winds. Deeper mixing in the wake of the cold front 
brings southwest wind gusts to around 25 kt across Saginaw Bay 
Thursday so a Small Craft Advisory is in effect through this 
evening. A stronger cold front then tracks southward across the 
region on Friday. This brings gusty north and northeast wind that 
shifts northwest and weakens by Saturday. Additional light rain will 
accompany this frontal passage.
